title: Customizing Existing Components
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of customizing existing components and when it is appropriate.
Apply component base classes using the documented Bootstrap 5.3 pattern.
Check modifier classes and variants and identify one likely failure mode.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will study customizing existing components and connect it to a small implementation or review task. The included subtopics preserve the attached Bootstrap curriculum outline.
content.why_it_matters: Customizing Existing Components is a customization capability. Prefer built-in utilities first, then CSS variables for local changes, and Sass/build customization only when the design needs generated framework changes.

content_blocks.text: Use the pinned Bootstrap 5.3.x baseline, follow the official component documentation, and verify semantic HTML, responsive behavior, and keyboard access before reusing the pattern.

content.task: Apply customizing existing components in a small branch or throwaway build. Compare the output before and after the change and record when this approach is preferable to a built-in utility.

common_mistakes.problem: Treating customizing existing components as a visual-only change.
common_mistakes.why: A class or style does not automatically add semantic meaning, application logic, or secure server behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Use the appropriate HTML semantics and verify the actual interaction.

common_mistakes.problem: Checking only the default viewport or happy path.
common_mistakes.why: Responsive changes and interaction states can reveal issues that are not visible in a single screenshot.
common_mistakes.fix: Repeat the task at a narrow and a wide viewport and include keyboard/error state checks where relevant.
